items.text: each scene in the Scenes list shows its palette on its picture: tap it to choose a palette for that scene (any scene, the studio's too), go back to its own colors, or open the palettes
a scene's name is one smaller line, with its icons under it
the palette strip is quieter: no grey outline round a color, and the names are smaller and sit lower
the ↔ that marks a color following another is a small quiet mark, no longer a pill that looks like a button
the ground's gradient can turn: Turn spins it once in 32, 16, 8 or 4 bars of the tempo, or holds still
tap a gradient's arrow again to turn it round; the lit arrow points the way the gradient runs
the ground gradient's slider has two handles: the line is where the two grounds meet, the circle how gently (drag it away from the line to soften)
the Color mixer is the Color editor: its button in the color row says editor, and Editor comes first at the panel's foot, then Color palettes
on a Mac trackpad the Color panel scrolls from anywhere: a scroll that began over a row of color chips caught on the row and moved nothing
the color shelf under the bar keeps its place: it jumped back to the start whenever the robot changed scene, so a chip far along (Pattern) could not be reached
Save to my colors is a plus under the big color circle

scrolling the Color panel on a phone or iPad: a finger that rested on a color chip before scrolling picked the color up instead of scrolling. Picking a chip up now takes a half-second hold, and any scroll wins
the plus on the big color circle is small and sits inside it, with a larger touch area
the × no longer sits on the ↔ that marks a color that follows another: the ↔ is at the bottom centre of the swatch

Ground 2. The ground can have a second color: as a gradient from Ground 1 to Ground 2 (down, across, corner to corner, the other corner, or from the middle out; softness is how gently they meet), or taking turns on the tempo (every 2 bars, bar, 2 beats or beat; softness is how slowly one fades into the other). Its mix sits under Ground 2 and between the two in the palette, and scenes and palettes keep it

blend by layer. Ink 1, Ink 2 and Touch share one blend; Arrows and Pattern each have their own; the grounds blend only with a camera, video or picture, now with multiply, screen, soft light, difference and color besides under, overlay and ignore
the chosen color in the palette strip has an × on its top right: tap it to clear that color (Ink 1, Ink 2, Touch, Arrows, Pattern, Ground 2)
while the robot holds your colors, the scene's name beside the palette is a link: tap it to wear that scene's colors
the Palettes view has its title, Color · Palettes, top left
the Color and Sound panels glide to a new height instead of jumping
the color editor's head: the swatch on the left; beside it # hex, on/off, follows and save in one row, and lightness, chroma and hue under it; the chips and Animation follow as their own groups
Save to my colors is a plus on the big color circle; Save palette is a round plus
in the palette strip the grounds read Bg 1 and Bg 2, so every name fits
scroll bars follow the light or dark chrome, and a hairline like the foot's sits above the scrolling part
the ring's drift says its period (32 bars, 16, 8, 4) like the panel

every color animation keeps time with the tempo (tapped, or the beat that plays; 120 a minute until there is one). Speed is a choice of periods: Drift turns in 32, 16, 8 or 4 bars; Breathe breathes in 4 bars, 2 bars, a bar or 2 beats; Pulse and Shuffle come every 2 bars, bar, 2 beats or beat
the little robot beside the palette's name shows the robot alone, and keeps animating while the scenes change
the Color panel has two views at its foot: Palettes, every palette in one list (find by name, yours or the studio's, A–Z or newest; wear, rename, delete), and Editor
palettes can be renamed, in the list or with the pencil beside the name; renaming a studio palette makes it yours under the new name
new and duplicated palettes are numbered (Sea Green 2, My palette 3), never "copy"
while the robot changes scenes, a small robot and the scene's name sit beside the palette's name, on one line that never moves the panel
Save palette, Save to my colors, Shuffle, Adjust, Duplicate and Delete have icons
Ink mix is three pills: grain, speed, tempo
the Blend heading lines up with the rest
the Color panel's spacing, cleaned up: one gutter, one kind of label, the same space between every group, a line between the palette and the editor
the sliders are a groove with a small knob inside it, like the switches, with room between them; chroma reads 0–100%, like lightness
Follows is one choice ("complement of Ink 1") beside the hex code; Ground's Auto is a switch
Ground is last in the palette: Ink 1, mix, Ink 2, Touch, Arrows, Pattern, Ground
swatches sit on one row that slides sideways
Shuffle is an animation: on the beat a color takes another of the palette's (Speed: every 8, 4, 2 or 1 beats)
drag a color chip onto the palette to give that slot its color; drag one slot onto another to swap them (on a phone, hold a moment first, so a swipe still scrolls)
while the Color panel is open, the robot keeps changing scenes but leaves your colors, their mix and animation alone (it was bringing each scene's own mix); the strip says so
Ink mix sits under Ink 2, where its colors are, and its chip sits between Ink 1 and Ink 2 in the strip; its own tab is gone
an empty Ink 2 is a circle with an ×
palette tools: shuffle the colors among the slots, adjust hue, saturation and lightness of the whole palette, duplicate, delete
the lit ring around a chosen swatch is no longer cut at the edge
the tempo goes down to 20 a minute (was 40); a pause of over three seconds between taps starts a new run

palettes. The Color panel opens on the palette: one strip of its colors in order (Ink 1, Ink 2, mix, Touch, Ground, Arrows, Pattern); tap one to edit it below. Its name opens the palettes, eight from the studio and your own: a tap wears one

Follows: a color can be tied to another, the complement of Ink 1, a deep or pale version, lighter, darker, warmer, cooler; change that one and the tied ones move with it. One color, related is a palette made this way
Save palette keeps the colors and their ties; a scene saved with a palette points at it, so changing the palette changes every scene that uses it
